headline: Asia took the baton in the AI unwind — Korea fell 7.6% in a session — while the dollar's bid finally broke and crude quietly deflated.
summary: The de-rating that started in US semis migrated overnight to the source. KOSPI fell 7.6% in one session to 5554, a 1-month move z of -2.35 and -16.2% on both the week and the month; EWY is -13.0% on the week and -9.3% on the month. Nikkei -4.9% with acceleration z=1.16, TAIEX -3.4%, Shanghai -1.6% and now at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range. This is not yet a global de-rating: Taiwan is still +3.2% on the month with relative strength up and EWT sits at the 88th percentile, while Korea's memory complex is the epicentre (MU -16.0% on the week, AVGO -8.0%, ASML -8.6%, SOXX -10.9%). The US tape going in was already soft — SPX 7718.9 (-1.1%), NDX -2.0%, SMH -4.0% — so Asia is catching down to Tuesday's US leadership break, not leading it.

Two offsets showed up today that were absent yesterday. First, the dollar bid broke: DXY -0.5% to 102.02 after printing 102.53 with acceleration z=1.24 a day earlier; EURUSD +0.2% to 1.1222 off its 7th-percentile lows, USDCHF -0.4%, USDCAD -0.2%, USDINR -0.2%. Metals immediately reflated — gold +1.8% to 4180.7, silver +2.4%, platinum +1.4% — reversing a chunk of Tuesday's violent dollar-driven flush. Second, the inflation impulse at the margin is deflating: WTI -1.4% to 93.76 and -11.4% on the month with acceleration z=-2.55, Brent -4.0% on the month, RBOB -5.3% today and -10.9% on the month, corn -10.2% (acc z=-2.35), wheat -7.7%. Breakevens refuse to move (5y 2.36%, 10y 2.35%). The hot CPI that drove yesterday's front-end repricing is being contradicted in real time by the commodity complex.

It is not a clean risk-on dollar decline. AUDUSD -0.9%, AUDJPY -1.2%, CEW -0.2%, EEM/SPY -3.5% on the week — the risk crosses kept bleeding while the dollar eased, which is the signature of position unwind, not appetite. The rates composite at -62 is the real constraint: 10y real yields at 2.84% (+24bp on the month, 91st percentile), the 30-year mortgage at 7.40% with z=2.06 and acceleration 1.50, 3m bills at the 100th percentile, 2s10s compressed to 37bp. Liquidity is being drained in the background: TGA +5.5% on the day to $920bn, +11.9% on the month, with RRP at 0.2bn and no buffer left.

Internals are where the risk sits. IWM/SPY is at the 4.5th percentile with z=-1.87, RSP/SPY the 17th, KRE/SPY the 16th, XHB/SPY the 0th. Credit is bending, not breaking: HYG at 76.81 with z=-1.16 and the 28th percentile, HYG/IEF -1.1% on the week, LQD at the 14th. And hedges remain mispriced against the visible stress — VIX 17.57 is only the 23rd percentile and VIX3M the 12th, while SKEW sits at 157.3 (87th percentile), MOVE at 99 (+18.1% on the month) and the VIX term structure is turning up at 0.898. The defensive bid is doing the index's work: XLV at the 97th percentile with relative strength turning up, QUAL at the 96th. Energy is now the crowded cyclical long most exposed to the crude roll — XLE at the 100th percentile, 19.2% above its 200-day, with the underlying barrel accelerating lower.

good.text: The dollar's bid broke after a month-long squeeze: DXY -0.5% to 102.02, EURUSD +0.2% off the 7th percentile, USDCHF -0.4%, USDCAD -0.2%. That is immediate relief for EM carry and metals.

The inflation impulse is deflating from the commodity side: WTI -11.4% on the month with acceleration z=-2.55, RBOB -10.9%, corn -10.2%, wheat -7.7%, with 5y breakevens parked at 2.36%. The CPI scare is not confirming in the inputs.

The long end is being bought: 30y -4bp today and -15bp on the week to 5.52%, 10y -9bp on the week, TLT +2.3% on the week. Duration is finally absorbing the growth doubt rather than selling with equities.
Precious metals snapped back hard off the flush — gold +1.8%, silver +2.4%, platinum +1.4% — a one-day reversal of Tuesday's dollar-driven liquidation in the metals complex.
Copper/gold still sits at the 92nd percentile with z=0.95 and acceleration 0.80, copper +3.0% on the month. The cleanest cyclical signal in the book still says repricing, not recession.
Brazil keeps compounding against the EM wreckage: EWZ +12.9% on the month (94th percentile), Bovespa z=1.92, USDBRL -2.2% on the month with the real still firm.

bad.text: Korea is in a disorderly unwind: KOSPI -7.6% in a session, z=-2.35, -16.2% on the week and month, 14.5% below its 200-day; EWY -13.0% on the week. Nikkei -4.9% alongside. Accelerating sell-side, not stabilisation.

The rates composite at -62 is the binding constraint. The 30-year mortgage is 7.40% with z=2.06 and acceleration 1.50, 10y real yields 2.84% (+24bp on the month), 2y 4.82%, 3m bills at the 100th percentile of the year.

Breadth is rotting beneath a 93rd-percentile index. IWM/SPY z=-1.87 at the 4.5th percentile, RSP/SPY the 17th, KRE/SPY the 16th, XHB/SPY the 0th. Only mega-cap defensives and energy are holding the tape up.

Credit is leaking quietly: HYG z=-1.16 at the 28th percentile and rolling over, HYG/IEF -1.1% on the week, LQD at the 14th percentile. This is the card that turns a leadership de-rating into an index event.
Liquidity is draining with no cushion left: TGA +5.5% today to $920bn and +11.9% on the month, while the RRP facility is empty at 0.2bn. Every dollar of cash build now comes straight out of reserves.

Hedges still underprice the stress: VIX 17.57 at only the 23rd percentile and VIX3M at the 12th, versus SKEW 157.3 (87th) and MOVE 99, +18.1% on the month. Complacency in spot vol with tail demand already bid.

trades.name: Own equity vol into cheap spot
trades.line: Buy VIX Dec 20/30 call spread + Dec SPX 5% OTM put spread
trades.expr: VIX Dec 20/30 call spreads sized 30-50bp of NAV, funded partly by selling 1-month 25-delta SPX calls; alternatively Dec SPY 735/690 put spread.
trades.thesis: Spot vol is priced for a calm tape that no longer exists. SKEW at the 87th percentile and MOVE at 99 say the institutional bid for tails is already there; VIX at the 23rd percentile and VIX3M at the 12th say the front of the curve has not repriced. Convexity is cheap relative to a leadership unwind now spreading across time zones.
trades.trigger: VIX +4.1% to 17.57 and the VIX/VIX3M term structure +5.6% to 0.898 and turning up, on a day KOSPI fell 7.6% (z=-2.35) and SOXX is -10.9% on the week.
trades.stop: VIX closes below 15 with term structure back under 0.85 and HYG/IEF reclaiming its weekly high — the unwind has been absorbed.
trades.target: VIX 24-26 and term structure above 1.00; 2-3x on the call spread.

trades.name: Health care over discretionary
trades.expr: Long XLV, short an equal dollar amount of XLY. Overlay: long LLY, short HD for a higher-beta version of the same leg.
trades.thesis: The defensive rotation has leadership characteristics, not just hiding-place characteristics: XLV is at the 97th percentile with relative strength turning up and acceleration z=0.71, while the consumer is being squeezed by a 7.40% mortgage and a 30-month-low discretionary/staples ratio.
trades.trigger: XLV +2.5% on the day and +4.1% on the month with LLY +3.6% and UNH +4.7%; XLY/XLP at the 3.6th percentile of its 52-week range, HD -4.9% and MCD -7.4% on the month.
trades.stop: XLV relative strength rolls over (1-month rs below zero) or the pair gives back 5%.
trades.target: +7-8% on the pair over the horizon; XLY/XLP making a new cycle low first.

trades.name: Fade E&P beta, keep the majors
trades.line: Short XOP / long XOM as crude accelerates lower
trades.expr: Short XOP (or buy Dec XOP puts), long XOM against it, roughly 1:1 dollar. Size 1/3 of a full position given energy's momentum.
trades.thesis: Energy equities are priced at the top of their 52-week range while the barrel is falling fast. E&P beta carries the highest operating leverage to a $94 WTI print and a collapsing crack; XOM is the quality anchor with relative strength still turning up, so the pair isolates the de-rating without fighting the sector's cash returns.
trades.trigger: WTI -1.4% to 93.76, -11.4% on the month with acceleration z=-2.55; RBOB -5.3% today and -10.9% on the month; yet XOP sits at the 97.5th percentile and 19.8% above its 200-day, XLE at the 100th.
trades.stop: Brent reclaims 110 or WTI closes above 100 — supply shock back in control; or the pair loses 6%.
trades.target: XOP back to its 200-day, roughly -12% absolute, 8-10% on the pair.

trades.name: Regional banks into a flattening curve
trades.line: Short KRE vs long SPY; curve flattening + credit leak
trades.expr: Short KRE against a long SPY hedge of equal notional, or buy KRE Jan 65/55 put spreads.
trades.thesis: Banks need steepness and credit calm; they are getting neither. The front end is pinned at 52-week highs on hike odds while the long end rallies, and high yield is quietly rolling over — the exact combination that compresses NIM expectations and re-opens credit-cost worries at the regionals.
trades.trigger: 2s10s -5bp to 37bp (-14bp on the week) with acceleration z=1.02; KRE -7.0% and KBE -7.8% on the month; KRE/SPY at the 16th percentile with z=-1.11; HYG at the 28th percentile.
trades.stop: 2s10s steepens back above 55bp or KRE/SPY reclaims its 1-month high.

trades.name: Brazil over Mexico
trades.line: Long EWZ / short EWW; BRL strong, MXN cracking
trades.expr: Long EWZ, short EWW, equal dollars. FX purists can express it as short USDBRL / long USDMXN in 1-month forwards.
trades.thesis: Latin America has split cleanly. Brazil is compounding on a firming real with the index at the 94th percentile and relative strength turning up; Mexico is being hit by the single most extreme FX move in the book, which is already dragging on local equity.
trades.trigger: USDMXN +0.5% today to 18.464, +7.8% on the month with z=2.91 and acceleration 1.76; USDBRL -2.2% on the month; EWZ +12.9% on the month (z=1.46) versus EWW -2.8% and rolling over.
trades.stop: USDBRL breaks above 5.25 (+4%) or EWZ 1-month relative strength turns negative.

trades.name: Housing, where 7.40% actually bites
trades.line: Short ITB; mortgage rate z=2.06 and still accelerating
trades.expr: Short ITB outright, or buy Jan ITB 80/70 put spreads; single-name version short DHI.
trades.thesis: The mortgage rate is the cleanest transmission of the CPI-driven real-yield move, and it is still accelerating. Housing equities already sit at the bottom of their range, but affordability at 7.40% has not been earnings-tested yet — estimate cuts come after the price break, not before.
trades.trigger: 30-year mortgage 7.40%, +69bp on the month with z=2.06 and acceleration 1.50; ITB -6.6% on the month at the 0th percentile; XHB/SPY at the 0th percentile; DHI at the 5th.
trades.stop: 10-year yield closes below 4.95% or ITB reclaims its 200-day (currently 13% above spot).

trades.name: Korea capitulation bounce
trades.line: Small long EWY vs short EWT into a 2.35-sigma flush
trades.expr: Buy EWY November calls or a small cash long, hedged with a short in EWT; quarter-size, add only on stabilisation.
trades.thesis: A 7.6% single-day index drop with a z of -2.35 is liquidation, not information. The won has not broken (USDKRW still -9.5% over three months) and Taiwan, the other half of the same supply chain, is up 3.2% on the month with relative strength up — the dislocation is positioning-driven and should partly reverse.
trades.trigger: KOSPI -7.6% to 5554, -16.2% on the month and 14.5% below its 200-day; EWY -13.0% on the week while EWT holds the 88th percentile.
trades.stop: USDKRW above 1380 (acceleration z is already 1.44) or EWY closes below 150.
